name: Sona Masoori Rice
description: Sona Masoori is the medium-grain, lightly aromatic rice that most Karnataka homes cook every day, and much of it is milled around Gangavathi, close to Hospet. Steamed (boiled) sona masoori cooks fluffy and separate, suits plain rice, bisi bele bath and pulao, and a 5 kg bag lasts a small family two to three weeks.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — local mill steam sona masoori sells at about ₹65–70/kg loose or in 5 kg bags; packaged national brands list higher (₹617–699 for 5 kg on flipkart.com / pricee.com, Aug 2026)
notes: Close-up of raw sona masuri grains from Wikimedia Commons; Open Food Facts India packs (Daawat 8901537074415, Vedaka 8903023009864) are available as branded alternatives if a pack shot is preferred.

name: Sona Masoori Rice
description: The same everyday medium-grain sona masoori rice in a full 25 kg mill bag, the size most households around Hospet buy for the month. Steamed sona masoori cooks light and separate for plain rice, chitranna and bisi bele bath; a 25 kg bag lasts a family of four roughly a month to six weeks.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/40018886/bb-royal-sona-masoori-steam-rice-25-kg-bag/ (₹1,500; BB Popular 25 kg lists ₹1,263) — local Gangavathi mill bags sell at about ₹1,400–1,700 depending on age and grade
notes: Photo shows an open jute sack of white rice in an Indian market; landscape framing.

name: Basmati Rice
description: Long-grain, fragrant basmati rice that cooks up long and separate, kept in Karnataka homes for biryani, ghee rice, pulao and festival meals rather than daily rice. A 1 kg pack covers two or three special-occasion meals for a family.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/280154/india-gate-basmati-rice-dubar-1-kg-pouch/ (India Gate Dubar 1 kg, MRP ₹159; India Gate Classic 1 kg is MRP ₹260)
notes: Front pack shot of India Gate Dubar 1 kg (India). Unbranded alternative: Commons File:Basmati_Rice_India,_raw.jpg (CC BY 2.0, cookbookman17).

name: Idli Rice
description: Short, plump parboiled rice (idli akki in Kannada) that is soaked and ground with urad dal for soft idli and dosa batter. A 5 kg bag keeps a family in idli and dosa batter for about a month of weekend breakfasts.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/10000414/bb-royal-idli-rice-5-kg-pouch/ (₹250; BB Popular 5 kg ₹249) — loose idli/boiled rice at Hospet kiranas is around ₹45–55/kg
notes: No India-market idli rice pack on Open Food Facts (only US 4 lb packs) and no Commons file titled idli rice; used a close-up of boiled ponni rice, the same parboiled short-grain type sold as idli rice.

name: Whole Wheat Atta
description: Finely milled whole wheat flour (godhi hittu in Kannada) for soft chapati, phulka and poori, and for the wheat dosa and holige made in North Karnataka homes. A 5 kg pack gives a family of four roughly three to four weeks of daily chapatis.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/126903/aashirvaad-atta-whole-wheat-5-kg-pouch/ (listed ₹277 at 15% off, implying MRP about ₹325; Sept 2026)
notes: Front pack shot of Aashirvaad Superior MP Atta 5 kg (India).

name: Whole Wheat Atta
description: Whole wheat flour (godhi hittu) in a 10 kg bag for households that make chapati or roti every day, along with poori, paratha and holige. A 10 kg bag lasts a family of four about six to eight weeks and works out cheaper per kilo than smaller packs.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/126906/aashirvaad-atta-whole-wheat-10-kg-pouch/ (₹546; other listings quote MRP ₹489–593 depending on variant and region, Sept 2026)
notes: Front pack shot of Aashirvaad Superior MP Atta 10 kg (Tamil-label pack, India).

name: Maida
description: Refined white wheat flour milled with the bran and germ removed, giving a fine, soft flour. Karnataka homes use it for the outer cover of holige (obbattu), Mangalore buns, samosa and bajji batter, and for bakery-style baking; a 500 g pack suits a family that fries or bakes only now and then.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — loose or local-mill maida sells at about ₹45–55/kg; packaged 500 g packs (Fortune, Pillsbury, regional mills) list around ₹35–45
notes: Pile of maida on a banana leaf, landscape framing. Open Food Facts pack alternatives (India): Good Life Maida 8902901001730, Fortune Maida 8906008811117.

name: Rava / Sooji
description: Coarsely ground wheat semolina, called rave in Kannada and sooji or Bombay rava elsewhere. It is the base of upma, kesari bath, rava idli and rava dosa; a 500 g pack covers several breakfasts for a small family.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/40293256/aashirvaad-double-roasted-suji-rava-less-moisture-more-quantity-made-from-mp-wheat-500-g/ (listed ₹41.8 discounted, implying MRP about ₹48; Sept 2026) — loose mill rava at kiranas is about ₹40–50/kg
notes: Front pack shot of Aashirvaad Double Roasted Suji Rava 500 g (India). Fortune Suji 500 g (8906008811131) is an Open Food Facts alternative; much rava in Hospet kiranas is sold loose.

name: Poha / Avalakki
description: Flattened parboiled rice flakes, called avalakki in Kannada, that soften after a quick rinse. They go into avalakki bath (poha upma), gojjavalakki, mosaru avalakki and festival offerings; a 500 g pack makes four to six breakfasts.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — loose medium/thick avalakki sells at about ₹60–80/kg; Tata Sampann and Fortune 500 g packs list around ₹45–65
notes: Close-up of raw poha flakes, landscape framing. Open Food Facts pack alternatives (India): Tata Sampann Poha 8904043902326, Fortune thick poha 8906008812817.

name: Ragi Flour
description: Finely milled finger-millet flour, ragi hittu in Kannada, the base of ragi mudde eaten with saaru across North Karnataka and of ragi rotti, dosa and morning ganji. A 1 kg pack gives a family several rounds of mudde or a few weeks of ganji.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — loose mill ragi flour around Hospet is about ₹55–70/kg; packaged 1 kg brands (Manna, 24 Mantra, Vedaka) list ₹80–110
notes: Ragi flour in a steel bowl, landscape framing, lighting is a little dim. Open Food Facts pack alternatives (India): Vedaka Ragi Flour 8903023006757, Organic Tattva 8906055440377.

name: Toor Dal
description: Split pigeon pea, togari bele in Kannada, the everyday dal of Karnataka for saaru, sambar, huli and bisi bele bath. A 1 kg pack lasts a small family two to three weeks of daily cooking.
mrp_source: https://www.commodityonline.com/mandiprices/arhar-dal-tur-dal (all-India retail about ₹118/kg, 1 Sept 2026; Amazon 1 kg listing ₹130, Aug 2026) — loose dal at Hospet kiranas is about ₹110–130/kg, packaged Tata Sampann 1 kg lists higher
notes: Dal spilling from a bowl on a white background, landscape framing. Alternatives: Commons File:Straucherbsen_(Toor_Dal)_in_einem_indischen_Supermarkt.jpeg (public domain, portrait, shop bin); Open Food Facts Tata Sampann Unpolished Toor Dal 8904043926216.

name: Urad Dal
description: Skinned split black gram, uddina bele in Kannada, ground with rice for idli, dosa and vada batter and used whole in the tadka for chutneys and upma. A 500 g pack is enough for two or three batches of idli batter.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — white urad dal sells loose at about ₹130–150/kg; Flipkart 500 g packs list about ₹62–75
notes: Skinned urad in a bowl on white, landscape framing. Open Food Facts pack alternatives (India): Good Life Urad Dal 8902901027280, 24 Mantra Organic Urad Dal White Split 500 g 8904083505914.

name: Moong Dal
description: Split, skinned yellow moong, hesaru bele in Kannada, which cooks quickly and soft. It is used for kosambari, moong dal payasa, pongal and light dal or kootu; a 500 g pack covers several such dishes for a family.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — mandi rate about ₹98/kg (commodityonline.com, Sept 2026), loose retail about ₹120–140/kg
notes: Portrait shot of moong dal in a glass; carries a small photographer watermark at the bottom edge. Open Food Facts alternative (India): Tata Sampann Unpolished Moong Dal 8904043926315.

name: Chana Dal
description: Split Bengal gram, kadale bele in Kannada, used for the holige (obbattu) filling, kosambari, vada, chutney tempering and dal. A 500 g pack covers one festival's holige or several weeks of everyday tempering.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — chana dal sells loose at about ₹80–95/kg; Flipkart 2 kg packs list about ₹163
notes: Portrait shot of a pile of chana dal on a plain blue background. Open Food Facts alternative (India): Fortune Chana Dal 8906007286039.

name: Masoor Dal
description: Split red lentil, masoor bele in Kannada, which cooks in minutes without soaking and goes into quick dal, saaru and mixed-dal dishes. A 500 g pack suits a small family for a few weeks of occasional use.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — masoor dal sells loose at about ₹80–95/kg; Flipkart 2 kg packs list about ₹166–167
notes: Square close-up of red lentils. Open Food Facts pack alternatives (India): More Select Masoor Dal 8903023012147, Daily Good Masoor Dal 8909177015508.

name: Kabuli Chana
description: Large white chickpeas, kabuli kadale in Kannada, soaked overnight and pressure-cooked for chole, sundal, usli and chana masala, or added to pulao. A 500 g pack makes three or four family-size dishes.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — loose kabuli chana is about ₹130–160/kg depending on grain size; packaged 500 g packs list ₹75–110
notes: Chickpeas in a ceramic bowl, landscape framing. Open Food Facts pack alternatives (India): Fortune Kabuli Chana Whole 8906008815184, Organic Tattva 8906055440094.

name: Green Moong
description: Whole green gram with the skin on, hesaru kaalu in Kannada, soaked and sprouted for kosambari and usli or cooked whole for curry and palya. A 500 g pack gives a family several rounds of sprouts or curry.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — whole green moong sells loose at about ₹120–140/kg
notes: Whole mung beans scattered on white, landscape framing. Open Food Facts alternative (India): DMart Moong Whole 8903363010650.

name: Groundnut
description: Raw shelled groundnuts, kadalekayi beeja in Kannada, a North Karnataka staple that goes into chutney pudi, roasted for kadlekai chikki, fried as masala shenga, and tempered into chitranna and upma. A 500 g pack lasts a family a few weeks of everyday use.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 — loose raw groundnut around Hospet (a groundnut-growing belt) is about ₹130–160/kg
notes: Near-square shot of shelled peanuts in a bowl. Open Food Facts only had a Flipkart Grocery raw groundnut pack (8904293723375).

name: Sunflower Oil
description: Refined sunflower oil, suryakanti enne in Kannada, the everyday cooking oil in most Karnataka homes for tadka, frying and sabzi. A 1 L pouch lasts a small family one to two weeks.
mrp_source: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/274120/sunpure-refined-sunflower-oil-1-l-pouch/ (selling ₹181.5; pricehistory.app records MRP ₹185, Feb 2026; Flipkart ₹220) — Fortune Sunlite and Gold Winner 1 L pouches are in the same band
notes: Front pouch shot of Sunpure Sunflower Oil 1 L (India), the Karnataka-made brand most kiranas here stock.

name: Sunflower Oil
description: The same refined sunflower oil in a 5 L jar for households that cook and fry every day; it works out cheaper per litre than pouches. A 5 L jar lasts a family of four about a month to six weeks.
mrp_source: https://mysunpure.in/collections/oil (brand site MRP ₹872 for the 5 L can; BigBasket https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/274125/sunpure-refined-sunflower-oil-5-l-can/ shows MRP ₹1,125 selling ₹880.5, Zepto ₹825; Sept 2026 — MRP printed on the jar varies by batch)
notes: No Sunpure 5 L on Open Food Facts (only 1 L, 500 ml and 15 L), so the image is the Fortune Sunlite Refined Sunflower Oil 5 L jar (India), a brand also stocked locally.

name: Groundnut Oil
description: Filtered groundnut oil, kadalekayi enne or shenga enne in Kannada, the traditional cooking oil of North Karnataka with a nutty taste, used for frying, rotti-side dishes and pickles. A 1 L pouch lasts a small family one to two weeks.
mrp_source: https://www.zepto.com/pn/freedom-double-filtered-groundnut-cooking-oil-pouch/pvid/1349a97a-09a5-44ab-b217-facd6ac630ee (MRP ₹230; BigBasket sells ₹195, Flipkart ₹185; Sept 2026)
notes: Front pouch shot of Freedom Double Filtered Groundnut Oil 1 L (India). Gemini and Gold Winner groundnut oils are alternatives; Ras chekku groundnut oil 8908003473031 is another Open Food Facts option.

name: Coconut Oil
description: Pure coconut oil, tengina enne in Kannada, in a 500 ml bottle, used in Karnataka kitchens for seasoning, frying and coastal-style curries and just as often as a hair oil. A 500 ml bottle lasts a family a month or more of light cooking use.
mrp_source: https://budgetbazaar.online/product/parachute-coconut-oil-500ml-jaar/ (MRP ₹331, selling ₹310; Blinkit and Zepto cached listings show ₹290 for the 600 ml bottle; Sept 2026 — copra prices have risen through 2025–26, so check the printed MRP)
notes: Classic blue Parachute 100% Pure Coconut Oil bottle on a plain background (492 px wide; the OFF entry lists no pack size but the 500 ml bottle shares this design). KLF Coconad 1 L (8906002660704) is an edible-grade alternative on OFF.

name: Ghee
description: Clarified butter, tuppa in Kannada, spooned over hot rice with saaru or dal, used for holige, payasa and festival sweets, and for tempering. A 500 ml pack lasts a family about a month of everyday use.
mrp_source: https://www.etvbharat.com/en/state/karnataka-nandini-butter-and-ghee-prices-hiked-enn26072408144 (KMF revision, Jul 2026: Nandini ghee 500 ml pouch ₹358, PET jar ₹368; earlier trade listing MRP ₹325 at babutradingco.com)
notes: No Nandini ghee on Open Food Facts (search returned nothing, API intermittently unavailable), so the image is the Amul Cow Ghee 500 ml jar (India); Amul Pure Ghee 500 ml 8901262030540 is another option.
